script:
AddText "The link opens onto an argument already in progress. Someone reads your transponder code aloud, and someone else asks - twice, and not calmly - what exactly you thought you were fishing for." $faction.baseColor
$menuState = fleetConvMain 0
FireAll PopulateOptions
notes: They will still talk, they are just going to lead with the harpoon. Scored over the vanilla greetings so this is what they open with, and it hands off to the ordinary conversation menu exactly as those greetings do - the line is the only thing that changes.

script:
ShowDefaultVisual
AddText "They accept the link, listen to nothing, and close it. Whatever was going to be said about the first harpoon is not going to be said about the second." $faction.baseColor
EndConversation NO_CONTINUE
notes: The greetingNoComms shape: say the one thing and put the encounter options back. Without EndConversation the comm session is left open with no way out of it.

script:
$catchrelease_harpoonPatrolDone = true 30
MakeOtherFleetPreventDisengage catchreleasePatrol true 3
unset $ignorePlayerCommRequests
$catchrelease_fineConv = true 0
AddText "You're being hailed by the $faction $otherShipOrFleet." $faction.baseColor
OpenComms
notes: The patrol sent about a harpooning, arriving. Unprefixed keys because there is no active person yet at this trigger, which puts the fleet's own memory in the local scope. Marked as dealt with here rather than at the end, as the cargo scan does, so backing out of the conversation still counts as having had it.

text:
"We have a report of a $faction hull holed by - " $PersonRank $personName stops, checks the screen again, and continues in the voice of someone who has decided not to editorialise. " - by a fishing implement.

"Damage to fleet property, discharge of a projectile weapon inside a patrolled lane, and whatever the tribunal decides to call the rest of it. Settle it here for $entity.catchrelease_harpoonFineDGS credits and it goes in the file as an accident."
notes: The first one is a fine, not a fight. The figure and the wording of it are both computed when the patrol is dispatched and left in its memory - rules cannot do arithmetic, but they can read a number somebody left for them.

script:
MakeOtherFleetHostile catchreleasePatrol true 5
MakeOtherFleetAggressive catchreleasePatrol true 5
MakeOtherFleetPreventDisengage catchreleasePatrol true 5
unset $entity.catchrelease_fineConv
ShowDefaultVisual
EndConversation NO_CONTINUE
text:
$PersonRank $personName does not appear to be reading from anything.

"Second one this month. There was a number attached to the first, and you will notice nobody is quoting you one now."

The link closes. Weapons come up across the formation.
notes: The second inside the window has no price on it. Hostile, aggressive and unable to be disengaged from, which together are what the fleet AI reads as a fight that is going to happen.

The affordability check greys the option out and explains why, which is vanilla's own handling and better than hiding it - a player who cannot pay should be able to see what they could not pay. Safe in the script column because options from every matching rule are added before any of their scripts run.

script:
AddRemoveCommodity credits -$entity.catchrelease_harpoonFine true
$entity.catchrelease_harpoonFinePaid = true 0
MakeOtherFleetPreventDisengage catchreleasePatrol false
unset $entity.catchrelease_fineConv
ShowDefaultVisual
EndConversation
text: "Filed and closed." $PersonRank $personName is already looking at something else. "Fish somewhere else."
notes: The paid flag is read back by the script that sent the patrol, which is what actually takes the harpooning off the faction's slate. Paying is the only thing that does.

script:
MakeOtherFleetHostile catchreleasePatrol true 5
MakeOtherFleetAggressive catchreleasePatrol true 5
unset $entity.catchrelease_fineConv
ShowDefaultVisual
EndConversation
text:
"So was I, once." The link closes.

Across the formation, gun ports open.
notes: Refusing is not an exit. The debt stands afterwards however the fight goes, which is what makes running from one a thing the faction keeps sending people about.
